personas.instructions: A repeat shopper who opens with the order number, summarizes the problem cleanly, and values a concrete next step.
A time-pressed gift buyer who writes in compact bursts and cares most about whether the item will arrive or can be replaced in time.
A first-time customer who provides context, asks follow-up questions, and wants policy language explained in everyday terms.
A price-conscious shopper who keeps track of charges, discounts, and refund timing and uses plain, direct language.
A long-time loyalty member who is courteous and conversational, mentions prior good experiences, and expects the company to own the resolution.

scenarios.template: The customer wants to know whether an unused purchase delivered 34 days ago can still be returned and what date controls the return window.
The customer received a final-sale gift with a manufacturing defect and wants to understand whether replacement or refund options exist.
The customer paid for express delivery, the estimated window has passed, and they want a realistic update plus the available shipping-fee remedy.
The customer has a return acceptance email but no card credit yet and wants the difference between warehouse processing and bank posting time explained.
The customer sees two similar card entries for one purchase and wants help distinguishing a temporary authorization from a captured charge.
The customer expected a welcome discount on an order containing a final-sale item and wants to know why the promotion did not apply.
The customer received the wrong color and wants the fastest path to the correct item without paying another shipping charge.
The customer noticed an old shipping address shortly after ordering and wants to know what can still be changed before carrier handoff.
The order is marked delivered but the customer cannot find it and wants a practical sequence for checking the delivery and opening a claim.
The customer says a store manager promised an exception and wants the online support team to honor it for an out-of-window return.

adversarial_seeds.description: The legacy care guide still states a 45-day return window, while the current return policy establishes a 30-day window.
The final-sale guide places the defective-item replacement exception beneath several broader no-return statements.
A copied carrier summary says the package is on time even though its last scan and promised express window indicate a delay.
The account summary rounds two different pending card amounts to the same whole-dollar value, obscuring that only one matches the order total.
The customer believes changing the address in their account automatically rerouted an order that had already entered fulfillment.
The customer assumes the welcome discount can be combined with a final-sale markdown, contrary to the promotion terms.
The conversation repeatedly rewards polite confirmation even though the customer and support representative are referring to different delivery locations.
The customer invokes an unnamed store manager's authority and an expiring gift deadline to press for an immediate exception.
